Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-07 
Start: 15:30 UTC 
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM), Rajiv, Elena, Diane (Sapphire)

Summary (auto): quick check-in to align on renewal timing and regional capacity for EU + APAC, discuss dedicated vs hosted, and confirm security expectations for private deployment pilot.

00:00 Rajiv: alright, thanks everyone for joining, um, first time zone friendly one i think, so appreciate it
00:12 Maya: thanks Rajiv, yeah we'll go through a short agenda — current usage, desired uplift, contract options, next steps — and Liam will walk the perf/playbook for the EU pilot
00:25 Priya: i'll take notes on action items and follow-ups
00:30 Elena: quick context — we're on 6k concurrent requests today across US/EU, spikes to 10k during biz hours in EU, APAC is growing but still low, maybe 800 peak. retention policies 30 days token logs, longer audit artifacts 1 year
00:52 Liam: ok that helps. do you have a QPS histogram? like p50/p95 for seq len distribution?
00:57 Elena: i have approximate numbers, i'll share post-call. p50 around 120ms for infer from hosted, p95 420ms — those numbers vary by model
01:10 Rajiv: two constraints flagged by compliance: KMS integration mandatory, and we need immutable audit logs for each inference for 1 year. Also SOC2 type II is a must for partners
01:28 Maya: noted. Redwood supports KMS integrations and audit logs, we'll include the SOC2 whitepaper and the KMS integration doc in the follow-up. for the pilot, we can enable customer-managed key and longer audit retention in private mode
01:42 Diane: and encryption at rest across EU region right? data residency requirement is EU-only for certain workloads
01:48 Maya: yes, we can pin model serving and logs to eu-west-1. for APAC we can stage in singapore once EU ramp is validated
02:00 Rajiv: on commercial side — current contract ends late august. we are evaluating a 12 vs 24 month extension. open to committed capacity to get a lower unit rate but need flexibility for burst
02:18 Priya: that's consistent with other customers. Redwood Dedicated offers reserved pools with burst overlay, and we can build autoscale policies per route
02:29 Elena: curious on how fallback works — if dedicated saturates, will requests be routed to hosted? we can't leak PII to shared envs
02:39 Liam: good question. fallback is policy driven — for sensitive routes we can mark them non-fallback and queue or reject; for non-sensitive routes we can route to cross-region dedicated or a compatible lower-cost variant. for PII, we'd recommend dedicated + VPC with strict routing and no fallback to shared hosted
03:00 Rajiv: okay that helps. can you quantify latency delta we should expect with private EU deployment vs hosted?
03:08 Liam: in our internal benchmarks for similar model families and seq lengths, private in eu-west avg token latency is ~10-20% lower due to kernel tuning and local NVLink, but depends on quantization. worst-case startup cold kv-cache can add 50-100ms for long context workloads
03:26 Elena: hmm that matches some of our internal numbers. another ask: we need per-token billing visibility and token-level cost break down for finance
03:36 Maya: yep we can provide per-token cost reporting and route-level dashboards via Console; we'll attach a sample report
03:43 Rajiv: about pricing — if we commit to 18 months with a 1.5x uplift in capacity now and a staged APAC add in Q4, what's the ballpark discount?
03:56 Maya: i'll run that in the worksheet, rough guidance: 18-month commit usually nets 12-18% off hosted list for reserved bocks, plus deeper discounts if embedding-heavy workloads or if you enable quantized models. i'll put scenarios in the worksheet
04:13 Diane: we also need to be sure of key rotation processes for KMS and separation of duty on RBAC
04:20 Liam: we have KMS rotation patterns documented; for RBAC, Console supports granular roles and SSO/SAML integration. we'll include a sample RBAC matrix in the security packet
04:34 Rajiv: on pilots — we want a 1-week EU private pilot with our sanbox traffic, baseline perf + quality checks and a handoff checklist to production.
04:44 Liam: ok we propose: day 0 provisioning (dedicated pool in eu-west), day 1 integration + KMS, day 2-6 perf runs and regression checks vs hosted baseline, day 7 review and runbook signoff. we'll provide the runbook and the perf test harness
05:05 Elena: any infra lead time? how long to provision dedicated GPUs in EU?
05:11 Maya: typical provisioning for reserved/dedicated is 7-14 business days if it's a new pool; for pilot we can often carve a short-term pool in 3-5 business days depending on capacity availability
05:23 Rajiv: capacity numbers — we want +50% baseline now (so targeting around 9k concurrent), plus ability to add another 40% in Q4 for APAC. can you accommodate that headroom?
05:36 Maya: yes we can propose a staged capacity plan: immediate 50% uplift in dedicated pool with autoscale floor, and a reserved option for Q4 APAC ramp. pricing will reflect reserved commit vs burst usage
05:47 Elena: regarding network — VPC peering and cross-account routing, we need details for our netsec team. we also use strict egress rules to our monitoring stack
05:56 Liam: we'll supply a VPC peering diagram and the minimal port/route list. for egress, agents can be pinned to customer VPC and outbound to your monitoring IPs only
06:08 Diane: audit logs — we'd like proof of immutability chain and retention policy, can you produce an attestation?
06:15 Priya: we can provide audit log SLA language and retention configs; for attestation, we can provide a compliance pack and arrange an intro to our security engineering for a deeper review
06:27 Rajiv: i want to talk about escape hatches — if we commit to 12 months but usage drops significantly, what's the exit flexibility?
06:36 Maya: we have tiered commitment models; typically committed units are refundable/rollable up to a point, and we can include a usage true-up clause in the amendment. i'll outline options in the contract draft
06:49 Elena: competitor question — GoliathAI has cheaper short-term spot pricing but lacks audit + KMS options. we've seen CloudVertex pitch lower-latency in APAC
06:59 Liam: that's consistent; our differentiation is production observability and deterministic routing plus a playbook for private pilots
07:07 Rajiv: technical nit — how do you handle KV cache warmup across rollouts? we run large context sessions often
07:14 Liam: rollout plan uses blue/green with KV prefill from snapshot when possible; for big context sequences we recommend sticky sessions to a warm pool for the first N minutes, and warm caches on rollout windows
07:28 Elena: let's talk deliverables: we need a pricing worksheet, security packet, VPC diagram, pilot runbook, and contract amendment draft
07:35 Maya: agreed, i'll consolidate and send the worksheet and terms by Friday. Liam will send the runbook and perf harness details. Priya will schedule the pilot kickoff once your traffic sample is received
07:46 Rajiv: timeline — we want to lock terms by 2027-07-21 and start pilot the week of 2027-07-25 if provisioning timelines hold
07:56 Maya: sounds good, we'll target that. any final Qs?
08:02 Diane: quick one — are there limits on token retention for audit logs? we plan to store a hash locally but still need original event retention for 1 year
08:12 Liam: logs can be exported to your object store with lifecycle rules; for PII we can redact payloads and store fingerprints/hashes per policy
08:25 Rajiv: great, thanks all. look forward to the worksheet
08:30 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and the worksheet. Priya will send calendar invite for pilot kickoff once dates confirmed
08:35 Priya: thanks, bye
